ideas.risks: The dominance reduction may hide a boundary case: quotes at low times, M=0, zero S_j, or post-low coordinates might create a horizon constraint not represented by the cumulative x_i variables.
ideas.summary: Audit the solver's equal-low multi-low drought proof by deriving the full finite-prefix primal LP for h^M,0^{N_0},ell,0^{N_1},ell,...,0^{N_r},ell,0^L,h and explicitly eliminating dominated actions and dominated horizons. The target is to prove the exact reduction to variables x_i with constraints z >= S_j - ell sum_{i<=j} x_i and z >= (h-ell) sum_i x_i, including all capacities and strict-crossing left-limit conventions.
ideas.title: Promote Equal-Low Drought Formula
ideas.why_promising: This is the most immediate partial theorem from the solver attempt, and it would turn CL-048 from candidate into an accepted reusable regression test for the two-level gluing program.

ideas.risks: Unequal lows may be too broad for a closed form; small examples may show several active horizons and no simple last-low formula.
ideas.summary: Study a single drought with unequal lows, h^M,0^{N_0},ell_1,0^{N_1},ell_2,...,0^{N_r},ell_r,0^L,h. First restrict to two or three distinct low levels and derive the reduced action menu {ell_j^-, h^-}. Look for a PAVA-like pooling rule or for a minimal counterexample where an earlier low horizon binds even though the last low has the largest raw surplus.
ideas.title: Unequal-Low Droughts
ideas.why_promising: The equal-low proof's monotonicity is the fragile point; unequal lows are the next place genuine front-loading constraints should appear if the two-level recursion has real structure.

ideas.risks: Repeated droughts may be easy because later quote opportunities dilute or repair earlier debt; a naive additive lower bound is likely false.
ideas.summary: Analyze paths made of several low droughts separated by highs, such as h^{M_0},0^{N_1},ell,0^{L_1},h^{K_1},0^{N_2},ell,0^{L_2},h. Track how low-quote mass used to repair a low horizon creates persistent high debt at all later high-dominated horizons, and test whether the state can be summarized by a reflected surplus/debt variable.
ideas.title: Repeated-Drought Debt Recursion
ideas.why_promising: The global D_n=o(n) gluing question likely turns on whether many diluted local conflicts can accumulate through shared high debt; equal-low single-drought formulas provide a clean base case.

ideas.risks: A boundary-augmented certificate may become tautological or fail to imply actual D_n mass at comparable scales.
ideas.summary: Define a boundary-augmented prefix LP that keeps late shadow thresholds visible when studying an early prefix. For example, the separated-block obstruction 0^N,c_0,0^L,c_1 has D_m=0 on the short prefix but a real shadow c_1 objective. Formalize an augmented value that captures this shadow and test whether repeated augmented defects force comparable-scale finite-prefix D_n.
ideas.title: Boundary-Augmented Prefix LP
ideas.why_promising: Iteration 14 showed ordinary shorter-prefix D_m misses late shadow conflicts; augmenting the prefix objective may be the right way to localize cross-scale incompatibility without making the false boundary-defect claim.

ideas.risks: The two-level market structure may still admit a parity-like separator, so a proof attempt should actively search for moving-scale counterexamples.
ideas.summary: Attack the restricted conjecture: for two positive levels ell<h in the formal left-limit deterministic known-path model, does D_n=o(n) imply existence of a fixed sublinear envelope and hence an anytime o(T)-regret policy? Use the single-drought and equal-low multi-low formulas as local lemmas, then either prove a dyadic localization theorem or construct a moving-scale repeated-drought separator.
ideas.title: Two-Level D_n Gluing
ideas.why_promising: This is the smallest nontrivial instance of the projective-consistency problem; solving or refuting it would clarify whether D_n is a real characterization or only a necessary certificate.

ideas.risks: Computation may only reproduce known cases unless examples are designed to stress specific conjectures; numerical LP values also need proof before promotion.
ideas.summary: Build an exact finite-prefix LP solver for small paths in the formal left-limit model, preferably outputting primal marginals and dual horizon weights. Run it on unequal-low droughts, repeated diluted droughts, alternating two-level prefixes with varying ell/h, and small three-level paths. Ask explorers to extract human-readable certificates from surprising outputs.
ideas.title: Finite-Prefix LP Laboratory
ideas.why_promising: The current bottlenecks are structural guesses about which horizons bind. Exact small LP certificates can quickly falsify proposed recursions and suggest the correct active-set or pooling rule.

ideas.risks: The construction may only restate already known rare-event caveats unless it yields clean all-horizon expected-regret bounds.
ideas.summary: Use equal-low or unequal-low drought blocks as rare branches in a stochastic exogenous process: conditional on a rare event, insert a long block with large local D_n, but choose probabilities so p_i N_i=o(T_i). Compute whether essential-sup or post-history information-tail quantities stay large while pseudo-regret remains o(T).
ideas.title: Rare Hard Drought Branches
ideas.why_promising: This would stress-test any future information-tail necessity condition and sharpen the existing rare-history obstruction using the strongest current finite-prefix gadgets.
